title: Would you choose the higher return or the lower drawdown?
author: April-Zoe

comments.author: Icy-Weakness8310
comments.body:
Not financial Advice:

Quick answer: Subjective to your risk tasks and tolerance... with a twist.

People choose lower drawdowns especially strategy two for more liquidity. You have more option to diversity when drawdowns do occur. 

More returns... self explanatory (more money...duh..). 

Now for the twist:   
You have higher sharp for the bottom strategy, Nice.   
  
Next question I'd ask is what situation does each strategy work in well in?

replies.author: April-Zoe
replies.body:
Good take. I prefer less drawdown because risk management is the key in preserving capital but I’d put a small bag in more exciting strategies so in a way DCAin into different ones.

The strategies have been testen on BTC since 2020, so on a 6 year period so in bull and bear but I need to deploy agents to see how they perform now.

replies.author: Icy-Weakness8310
replies.body:
I've been asking this question around a lot especially for agent strategies for this subject amuses me a good amount. 

Do you mind sharing the execution data matched up with price?

For me in terms of btc I posted a while back on an issue after 2024 with a vol band strategy that on paper outpreformed every strategy... until you looked at performance over time.

However after the ETF legislation stuff, my other strategy started to completely crush the others. However on paper the one strategy that started working very well seemed unreasonable overall. After 2024, crazy alpha compared to others.

In terms of agents, I notoriously know from running an HMM/LSTM a while back on data that regime taste can change invalidating a good model or agents.

I'd love to see how your agents deal with these regime shifts. Do you mind sharing execution data?

replies.author: April-Zoe
replies.body:
That is a fair concern. A single aggregate backtest can hide exactly the kind of regime break you are describing.

Yes, I am happy to share the execution data matched against BTC price. I would separate it into three records: the trade level backtest with each entry and exit, the forward paper record from when the strategy started running, and actual Hyperliquid fills where it has traded live. Those should never be mixed together as if they prove the same thing.

But first my plan is to optimize the strategy so the drawdown is lesser even if the overall performance is a bit lower. Gotta take it to the smallest possible level. Then I'll start doing the forward paper record and after a month or two deploy an agent running a small capital allocation to see how it actually performs on HL. I'm building my strategies on a platform we're building with a small team, check my BIO if you want to see, it's published there. Or just DM me if you need more details. I'm happy to chat.

...

Regarding regime shifts, Trigr Agents do not automatically decide that the market has changed. In most cases, the Agent is a deterministic execution layer that follows the strategy’s defined rules. A strategy can include regime, volatility, time, and cross asset filters. The ML optimizer can also learn an entry gate using purged walk forward out of sample testing, leak checks, DSR, and PBO. However, the deployed model does not continuously retrain. Retraining creates a new model run that must be evaluated again. Which is imo actually a very smart thing to do especially with regime changes.

We are still in beta, so I do not want to overstate how much statistically meaningful live history exists for every strategy yet. But I agree that this is the right way to judge whether a strategy survived a regime change instead of simply fitting one.

I'm on my way to find that out ...
